The two functions answer different questions: "is any repo synced+enabled for this team" (the settings flag) vs "which config owns THIS PR" (the task). Provider gap: `installation_id` is read-only on the config serializer (views.py:196-199), so the only path that sets a non-blank `installation_id` is the sync flow, which hardcodes `provider="github"` (views.py:306-309) and sets `connected_by_user_id` (views.py:464). Every row that satisfies `has_reviewable_repo_config`'s filter therefore has provider="github"; adding `provider="github"` would be a no-op. Reader lag: the flag's sole consumer is `get_stamphog_connected` (products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:72-81), documented as a fail-soft "informational UI flag", and the only frontend use is a `disabledReason` on the toggle (products/review_hog/frontend/CodeReviewScene.tsx:1063-1069), which already keeps an on switch interactive when the flag is false. The task path is writer-pinned by explicit design because it gates run creation (tasks.py:1136-1138); a settings GET does not.
votes.refutation: Attempted to find a reachable trigger for each of the three claimed divergences. (1) Casing: refuted — the settings-flag query has no repository predicate at all. (2) provider: refuted — rows that pass the flag's filter necessarily carry a non-blank installation_id, which only the GitHub-hardcoded sync path can write, so no non-github row can ever make the flag true. (3) Reader lag: the worst case is a momentarily stale disabled-tooltip on an informational toggle immediately after first sync, self-healing on the next settings read; that is a cosmetic transient, not a correctness defect, and pinning it to the writer would add writer load to every settings GET for no user-visible gain. The finding's core premise (two surfaces evaluating the "same predicate" differently) is contradicted by the code: they are intentionally different predicates for different questions.

votes.refutation: Attempted to find a shared predicate that could drift: there is none. `has_reviewable_repo_config` is a team-level existence check with no repository or provider term, so casing cannot diverge, and provider is single-valued in production. The only remaining claim, reader replica lag, is reachable only when a separate `PRODUCT_DB_STAMPHOG_READER_URL` is configured, and its effect is confined to a transient stale `disabledReason` on an informational switch that self-corrects on the next read. No correctness, security, or data-loss consequence; the two surfaces answer different questions by design and the writer pin on the task path is documented. The finding is a duplicated-safeguard/style preference with a factually wrong premise.
